max_tire.note: Fits on stock coils once the steering stops are adjusted to stop rubbing at full lock; some owners squeeze in 265/75R16 with slight chassis rub cured by the stops.

Owners on a 2-in OME lift run either size with no trimming. Expect to wind the steering stops out; the 265s cost turning circle and some owners needed longer stop bolts to stop them hitting the radius arms.

items.title: Fuel tank bottom corrosion
items.summary: The bottom of the fuel tank can corrode over time and leak fuel.

items.title: Fuel filter bracket corrosion
items.summary: Corrosion can occur between the fuel filter and its retaining bracket.

items.title: Brake pedal pivot circlip
items.summary: A wrongly installed circlip can let the brake-pedal pivot shaft move out of position.

items.title: Seat belt retractor pivot pin
items.summary: An oversized nylon pivot pin in the retractor lock mechanism.

items.title: Rear brake line chafe
items.summary: The right rear metal brake line can rub on the top of the shock and leak one brake circuit.

items.title: Brake light switch
items.summary: The brake-lamp switch by the pedal may fail to operate.

timeline.change: Launched in June as a two-door: carburettored 3.5 Rover V8 (135 hp), coil springs, four-wheel discs and permanent dual-range 4WD with a manual centre diff lock.
Factory four-door arrives in July, following approved conversions such as Monteverdi's.
LT77 five-speed and separate LT230 transfer box replace the LT95 combined box.
ZF four-speed automatic replaces the three-speed Chrysler TorqueFlite; new instrument pod.
Lucas fuel injection replaces carburettors in most markets; VM 2.4 Turbo D diesel launched for Europe; facelift with plastic slatted grille.
Factory US imports begin 16 March 1987 — four-door only.
3.9 V8 replaces the 3.5; Borg Warner chain transfer case with a viscous-coupling centre diff replaces the manually locked unit; VM diesel grows to 2.5.
108-in LSE (UK) / County LWB (US) with the 4.2 V8; Land Rover's own 200Tdi replaces the VM diesel.
Electronic air suspension arrives on high-end 1993 model-year trucks (mainly LWB). Rides beautifully; pumps, sensors and valve blocks fail, and many have since been coil-converted.
Renamed 'Classic' alongside the new P38A; Discovery-derived 'soft dash' fitted to run-out trucks; 300Tdi replaces 200Tdi late 1994.

identify.intro: Classics were built for 26 years in two- and four-door, two wheelbases, carb and injected, coil and air — and US buyers also meet grey-market and 25-year imports, so it pays to know what you're looking at.

items.head: US-spec vs grey market
items.body: Factory US imports began on 16 March 1987 and were four-door only. Any US two-door, any pre-1987 truck, and any diesel came in through grey-market converters in the early 1980s or as a later 25-year import.

items.head: Wheelbase and suspension
items.body: Standard trucks have a 100-in (2,540 mm) wheelbase. The LSE / County LWB (1992 on) has a 108-in (2,743 mm) wheelbase, the 4.2 V8 and electronic air suspension; check whether a previous owner has fitted a coil conversion.

items.head: Transfer case
items.body: Pre-1989 trucks have a manual centre-diff lock (vacuum servo on the LT95, mechanical on the LT230). From 1989 a chain-driven Borg Warner box with a viscous coupling locks automatically, and a seized coupling makes the truck scrub on tight turns.

items.head: Hard dash vs soft dash
items.body: Until 1994 the Classic kept its original hard-plastic 'Airfix' dashboard. Run-out trucks got the Discovery-derived 'soft dash' with Rover 800 switches, the version enthusiasts call 'soft dash' models.

items.head: CSK
items.body: The 1990 CSK, named for Spen King, ran to 200 UK-built trucks: Beluga Black paint, chrome bumpers, silver coachlines, a recalibrated 3.9 V8 (185 bhp) and front and rear anti-roll bars. Australia separately built 400 CSKs based on the four-door Vogue.

values.intro: Prices are wide: rough coil-sprung SWBs and diesel projects are still cheap, clean County LWBs and two-doors bring real money, and V8-swapped restomods sit in their own price band.
values.note: Based on 20 Bring a Trailer sales between July and October 2026 ($5,500–$153,000, median about $24,000). Original-owner and low-mile County LWBs and a clean two-door sat at the top of the stock-truck range.

paragraphs: Land Rover didn't sell the Range Rover in the US until 16 March 1987, and then only as a four-door. In the early 1980s Americans bought grey-market trucks converted to US rules by Los Angeles-area dealers and, from 1984, by Aston Martin's US division. Two-doors, diesels (VM, 200Tdi, 300Tdi) and manual-gearbox Euro trucks were never US-market vehicles.

Every Classic is now more than 25 years old, so under NHTSA rules any of them can be imported without meeting FMVSS; the 25 years are counted from the manufacture date, and the truck is declared under Box 1 on the HS-7 form. State titling and emissions rules still apply, so check your state's requirements, especially California's, before buying a diesel or a carbureted import.

production.intro: Built at Solihull from 1970 to 1996, with CKD assembly in Australia (Enfield, 1979–1983) and Venezuela (Las Tejerías, 1973–1981).

community.note: UK club founded in 1985 for owners of every Range Rover from the Classic onward. It attends the major 4x4 and classic shows and runs camping events.

community.name: Association of North American Rover Clubs (ANARC)
community.note: Umbrella group for 24 North American Land Rover clubs. Its site carries member-club events, and it runs recovery and trail-leader training.
